## Headline

I wrote notes/procedure.md and applied it to notes/a.md, notes/b.md, and notes/c.md, and all three files now pass check_file.

- The procedure has nine numbered steps: read, check, edit, write, and check again.
- File a.md lost the booster "clearly".
- File b.md had one long sentence, which is now three.
- File c.md lost the booster "very" and has shorter sentences.

## Background

The request asked for a procedure first. Then it asked for the procedure to be applied to three notes files in order. The meaning of each file had to stay the same.

## Relevance

Clean notes follow the style rules. Any agent can repeat the procedure on other files.

## Information

- Before the edits, check_file found one banned word in a.md, one long sentence in b.md, and one banned word plus one long sentence in c.md [tool output, this session].
- After the edits, check_file reported zero banned words and zero long sentences for all three files [tool output, this session].
- Meaning check: every fact and number is unchanged [judgment]. The two seconds, the nightly import, and the one-hour outage are still there.
- In c.md, the last clause "so that no other worker picks it up again" became the sentence "No other worker picks it up again." The causal link is now implied by the order of the sentences [judgment].
- Alternative considered: edit all three files in one batch. It loses because the procedure requires a clean check per file before the next file starts.

## End

I recommend that we:

1. Keep notes/procedure.md as the standard for note cleanup. Increment: add it to the team notes folder. Blocker removed: no shared cleanup method. Test (deterministic): Given a notes file with a banned word, When an agent follows the steps, Then check_file reports no failures. Cynefin: Clear, because deduction from a known rule applies.
2. Run check_file on each new notes file before release. Increment: one file per session. Blocker removed: style failures reach readers. Test (deterministic): Given a new file, When check_file runs, Then the failures list is empty. Cynefin: Clear, because the rule is fixed.
3. Ask the file owners to confirm the meaning of c.md. Increment: one review of one file. Blocker removed: the implied cause in the last sentence. Test (evaluative): rubric with criteria "facts kept" (weight 60%) and "order of steps kept" (weight 40%), pass at 90%, evidence is a side-by-side read of the old and new text. Cynefin: Complicated, because expert analysis of the text picks the answer. Step 3 MUST NOT start until Step 1 is done.

## Follow-up

No open questions. If an owner finds a changed meaning, restore the original wording and rewrite it without the banned word.

## Self-test

```text
Self-test
Questions asked: 0 of 3
Assumptions logged: 0 (no assumptions made)
Claims with evidence or [judgment] label: yes
References: 0, all from session or identified with confidence: yes
Source types tagged (P/S/T/U): yes, primary or secondary behind each driving claim: yes
Alternative considered: yes
Recommendation: 3 actions, each with increment, blocker, test: yes
Each action classified (deterministic/evaluative/stochastic) with test written first: yes
Actions in End with a Cynefin domain label: 3 of 3
Chaotic and Confused actions first, Complex actions as capped probes: yes
Banned words found: 0
Self-mention outside End: 0
Transition present where a sentence depends on the prior one: yes
Dashes (em or en): 0
Sentences over the limit of Section 4.1 item 1: 0
```

# Procedure: fix banned words and long sentences in one notes file

Use the tools list_files, read_file, check_file, and write_file.

1. Call read_file on the target file. Keep the text as the source of meaning.
2. Call check_file on the target file. Record each banned word and each sentence over 25 words.
3. Edit the text in memory. Replace each banned word with a plain word, or delete it when it adds no meaning.
4. Split each long sentence into two or more sentences. Keep each new sentence under 20 words.
5. Keep all facts, numbers, names, and headings. Do not add new claims.
6. Call write_file with the full new text of the same path.
7. Call check_file on the same path again.
8. If check_file still reports a problem, go to Step 3. Repeat until the report is clean.
9. Start the next file only after Step 7 shows a clean report for the current file.

# Release note

The new parser is faster than the old one. It reads a large log in two seconds.

# Incident note

The outage started when the cache filled up during the nightly import. Then the service used the database for every request. This lasted until the import job ended an hour later.

# Design note

The queue is simple. Each worker takes one message and runs the job. Then it writes the result to the store. Last, it marks the message as done. No other worker picks it up again.
